title: Exactness closure of globally constructible pro-etale module sheaves
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Work in the abelian category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_Y$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Use precisely the global finite-stratification constructibility predicate [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], including a positive number of strata. If $f:F\to G$ is a morphism between constructible module sheaves, then $\ker f$ and $\operatorname{coker}f$ are constructible. If $S$ is a short exact sequence $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$ of module sheaves and $F,G$ are constructible, then $E$ is constructible. The scheme and the coefficient ring may be empty and zero, respectively.

proof.text: A finite coefficient ring is Noetherian: its ideals form a finite set. A finite module is generated by its finite underlying set, and a finitely generated module over a finite ring is finite, since a finite generating family presents it as a quotient of a finite power of the ring.

proof.text:
For every scheme map $f:X\to Y$, [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] identifies the specified $c^f_\Lambda$ with an isomorphism. Thus [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] supplies the exact module inverse image; after forgetting the module action it is the abelian inverse image. For a weakly etale $j:U\to X$, [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] identifies $j^*$ with localized restriction. Applying [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk] to the underlying abelian sheaf gives
$$(F|_U)_{\bar u}\cong F_{j\bar u}.$$
This stalk isomorphism is used below only for finiteness of underlying sets, so no scalar comparison beyond these identifications is required.

proof.text: Every geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ lifts to a member of any pro-etale covering $\{U_j\to X\}$. Indeed, base change along $\bar x$ gives a covering $\{U_j\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\}$ by the covering-preserving base-change functor of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Joint surjectivity in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] gives a point $v$ of some fibre. This fibre is weakly etale over $\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. Restricting to an affine neighbourhood of $v$ preserves weakly etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-source-locality]. There, [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field] makes $\kappa(v)/\Omega$ separable algebraic. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed this extension is $\Omega$ itself. Its point map gives a lift $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U_j$ over $X$. The same argument applies to coverings of every stratum.

source.place: Definition of covering families; more-algebra.tex Tag 092Q (lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field) for the fibre residue fields.

proof.text: On any scheme $T$, a locally constant sheaf $F$ has finite geometric stalks if and only if it admits finite constant local models. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction] and [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the localized constant module models in the definition are constant module sheaves on the members’ own pro-etale sites. Use the covering and module models $M_j$ of [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. If $U_j$ is nonempty, choose a point and an algebraic closure of its residue field, obtaining a geometric point $\bar u$ as in [def-weil-geometric-point]. Step 2 and [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk] identify $M_j\cong(F|_{U_j})_{\bar u}\cong F_{j\bar u}$, so finite stalks imply $M_j$ is finite. Empty members may be discarded. Conversely, for an arbitrary geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, step 3 gives a lift to some $U_j$. The same two stalk isomorphisms identify $F_{\bar t}$ with that finite $M_j$. This proves finiteness at every geometric point, rather than just at a chosen point of each member.

source.place: Tag 099Y (lemma-compare-locally-constant): constant local models; geometric stalk comparison as in Tag 0993 (lemma-classical-point).

proof.text: For any scheme map $f:X\to T$, inverse image preserves locally constant sheaves with finite stalks. Choose finite local models $M_j$ for $F$ by step 4. The hypotheses of [lem-exc-proetale-pullback-locally-constant] hold: the ring is finite, the pullback uses its specified canonical constant-ring map, and the local models are finite modules. Its displayed comparison gives finite constant models for $f^*F$ on the base-changed covering $\{X\times_TU_j\to X\}$. Step 4 then gives finite stalks at every geometric point of $X$. In particular this uses preservation of the same finite module values, rather than only preservation of local constancy.

proof.text: For $F,G\in\mathcal B$, choose the two finite stratifications in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection] to obtain their common finite stratification by fibre products. Each refined stratum maps to an old stratum through the corresponding projection. Composition of module inverse images [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition] identifies restriction from $Y$ with this successive pullback. Step 5 therefore shows that both restricted sheaves are locally constant with finite stalks on every refined stratum.

source.place: Tag 03RZ (lemma-constructible-abelian), common finite partition argument, carried out on the given global partitions.

proof.text: For a morphism $u:F\to G$ in $\mathcal B$, use the common stratification from step 6. By step 4 its two restricted sheaves have finite constant models, whose finite underlying sets generate them as $\Lambda$-modules. Thus they are locally constant of finite type. The module inverse image is exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so restriction of $\ker u$ and $\operatorname{coker}u$ is the kernel and cokernel of the restricted morphism. Transport the pro-etale site to its AsSmall model by precomposition. The forgotten constant commutative-ring sheaf and the constant RingCat sheaf have locally bijective units from the same constant ring presheaf, so sheafification gives the unique coefficient isomorphism compatible with constant sections. Scalar restriction along this isomorphism identifies their module categories. The module sheafification universal properties identify the corresponding constant modules, also on slices. Coverwise finite constant models on the terminal object give the generic local definition on every object by pullback of the cover, and the converse is its specialization to the terminal object. These site and coefficient equivalences preserve all finite limits and colimits. Thus apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-derived-serre] on the small model of each stratum, with the lifted coefficient ring $B=\Lambda$, Noetherian by step 1. The two resulting sheaves are locally constant of finite type. Each finitely generated local model is a quotient of $\Lambda^r$ for some finite $r$, hence finite as a set. Step 4 gives finite stalks at every geometric point. The same finite stratification therefore witnesses constructibility of both sheaves. For $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$, use the common finite stratification of the outside terms; exact restriction and the extension clause of the same lemma give locally constant finite-type restrictions of $E$. Their models and all geometric stalks are finite by the preceding argument. Thus $E$ is constructible. Together with step 1, this supplies all weak-Serre hypotheses for the global finite-stratification convention [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf].

lean.statement:
theorem constructibleProEtale_exactClosure
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] :
    (∀ (F G : proEtaleRingModules Y (proEtaleConstantRing Y A)) (f : F ⟶ G),
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A F →
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A G →
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A (kernel f) ∧
        IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A (cokernel f)) ∧
    (∀ S : ShortComplex (proEtaleRingModules Y (proEtaleConstantRing Y A)),
      S.ShortExact → IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A S.X₁ →
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A S.X₃ →
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A S.X₂)

The stalk of a constant local model is its underlying module, identifying finite models and finite stalks.
Canonical module pullback preserves the same finite constant values, so refinements preserve finite local constancy.
The generic finite common refinement is the fibre-product intersection of the two existing global partitions.
The generic finite-type local Serre theorem supplies the three exactness closures on each stratum; no other statement of the ambient-operations unit supplies it.
